segments.audience: Greensboro parents choosing a first martial arts class
segments.hypothesis: Showing parents what happens during a first visit will help more of them book.
segments.headline: Your child's first martial arts class can start with a free visit.
reasons: Beginners are welcome. Your child can try a class before you decide to enroll.
Parents can sit beside the training floor and watch the class.
Choose an available class and complete the visitor form before arriving.
Come ten minutes early in comfortable clothes to 719 W Gate City Blvd in Greensboro.
segments.proofNeeded: A current class photo approved for public use, confirmed class availability, and an anonymized parent inquiry about starting.
segments.next: Use the existing parent pilot as the baseline. Check booking attribution first. Review the page draft before proposing a separate landing-page test.

segments.audience: Local adults considering their first Tai Chi class
segments.hypothesis: A clear explanation of the first class will help interested beginners choose a visit.
segments.headline: Try a Tai Chi class in Greensboro.
reasons: You can start with no previous training.
Your first visit is free, so you can take a class before deciding to continue.
Check the available classes and complete the visitor form before coming.
Cloud Forest is at 719 W Gate City Blvd in Greensboro.
segments.cta: Choose a class for your free visit
segments.proofNeeded: Confirm the current beginner Tai Chi schedule and obtain a current class photo with permission to use it.
segments.next: Keep as an organic draft until the parent pilot is reviewed. Avoid medical or fitness outcome promises.

segments.audience: School owners doing tuition and attendance work after class
segments.hypothesis: Starting with a familiar office task will produce more qualified demos than a general feature tour.
segments.headline: Finish class with fewer office tasks left to sort out.
reasons: See attendance and school records together when deciding who needs a follow-up.
Review tuition, waivers, and the school's website in one system.
Ask Zeus to help work through the school records.
Check whether the workflow fits your school before committing to a subscription.
segments.proofNeeded: Record a working demo with sample school data. Collect an owner interview confirming which task costs the most time. Do not claim measured time savings yet.
segments.next: Review with one consenting owner. Pricing remains $99/mo or $990/yr for the first 20 schools; standard $169/mo or $1,690/yr. No setup fee. The 14-day trial requires a card. Check founding availability.

segments.audience: School owners evaluating software before a current contract ends
segments.hypothesis: A concrete transition discussion will get more replies from owners who cannot switch immediately.
segments.headline: Look at your next school system before your current contract ends.
reasons: Start with the attendance and tuition work you need the new system to handle.
See how DojoZeus brings school records and the website together.
Review the work needed to move your school before choosing a start date.
Confirm pricing and founding availability when you are ready to subscribe.
segments.proofNeeded: Verify supported imports, expected transition work, and the owner's contract timing. Do not promise free overlap, automatic imports, or a reserved founding price.
segments.next: Prepare a migration checklist from supported imports. Keep outreach in draft until approved.

segments.audience: Teachers with a workshop or lesson ready to put online
segments.hypothesis: Starting with one existing lesson will make the first school setup feel achievable.
segments.headline: Put your first lesson in a school with your name on it.
reasons: Start with a lesson you already teach.
Build your school free and review the paid plans before subscribing.
See a working school before deciding how to organize your own.
Choose the plan that fits how you want to teach and serve your members.
segments.cta: See how to start your school
segments.proofNeeded: A working sample lesson, a verified signup flow, and an interview with a teacher who already has interested students.
segments.primary: Verified signups that publish a lesson
segments.next: Show a working example to a consenting teacher. Record where setup becomes confusing. Free signups alone do not establish revenue.

segments.audience: Owner-operators managing truck records after a run
segments.hypothesis: A demo of one paperwork task will produce clearer buying signals than a broad platform pitch.
segments.headline: See how RigBoss handles the paperwork after a run.
reasons: Start the demo with a truck record you need to keep organized.
Review the workflow before deciding whether it fits your operation.
Keep your ELD in place while evaluating RigBoss.
Confirm the current plan and onboarding requirements on the product site.
segments.proofNeeded: A verified demo using sample records and an owner interview identifying the recurring paperwork problem. Avoid compliance guarantees.
segments.next: Confirm the exact supported workflow before recording the demo. Keep ads and outreach in draft.

segments.audience: Independent shop owners and service writers handling repair updates
segments.hypothesis: Showing a repair update will prompt more useful conversations than listing every feature.
segments.headline: Show a customer what is happening with the repair.
reasons: Start with a repair photo and the update a customer needs.
See the shop workflow in a demo before deciding whether it fits your service desk.
Check how the system handles the next step in the repair.
Review onboarding and the current offer on the product site.
segments.proofNeeded: A working demo with sample repair data, confirmed customer-update behavior, and an interview with a service writer. Do not claim recovered revenue without records.
segments.next: Verify the customer-update flow and record a short demo. Keep ads and outreach in draft.
